input_body: aad a pile :-- He mycelne aad gesomnode he gathered a great pile, Bd. 3, 16; S. 542, 22. v. ād.
aac, e; f. An oak: -- Aac-tūn Acton Beauchamp, Worcestershire, Cod. Dipl. 75 ; A. D. 727; Kmbl. i. 90, 19. v. Āc-tūn.
aar honour :-- In aar naman in honore nominis, Bd. 2, 6; S. 508, note 43. v. ĀR; f.
aaþ an oath :-- He ðone aaþ gesæh he saw the oath. Th. Dipl. A. D. 825; p. 71, 12. v. Āþ.

a-bacan, ic -bace, ðū -bæcest, -bæcst, he -bæceþ, -bæcþ, pl. -bacaþ; p. -bōc, pl. -bōcon; pp. -bacen To bake; pinsere, coquere :-- Se hlāf þurh fȳres hǳtan abacen the bread baked by the heat of fire. Homl. Pasc. Daye, A. D, 1567, p. 30, 8.

ABAL, afol, es; n. Power of body, strength; vigor, vires, robur corporis :-- Ðīn abal and cræft thy strength and power, Cd. 25; Th. 32, 9; Gen. 500. [Orm. afell: O. H. Ger. aval, n: O. Nrs. afl, n. robur, vis: Goth. abrs strong.]

a-bæligan; p. ode; pp. od To offend, to make angry; irritare, offendere :-- Sceal gehycgan hæleða Ǧghwylc ðæt he ne abælige bearn waldendes every man must be mindful that he offend not the son of the powerful, Cd. 217; Th. 276, 27; Sat. 195. v. a-belgan, a-bylgan.

a-began; p. de; pp. ed; v. trans. To bend, bend down, bow, reduce, subdue; incurvare, redigere, subigere :-- Weorþe heora bæc swylce abēged eāc dorsum illorum semper incurva, Ps. Th. 68, 24. v. bēgan.

expected_senses.gloss_en: To bend, bend down, bow, reduce, subdue

input_body: a-beātan; p. -beōt; pp. -beāten To beat, strike; tundere, percellere :-- Stormum abeātne beaten by storms, Exon. 21b; Th. 58, 26; Cri. 941. v. beātan.
abbod-hād. Add:-- Ðā ðe ðæne abbod tō abbodhade gecuron qui abbatem ordinant, R. Ben. 124, 16. Sē ðe tō abbodhade sceal qui ordinandus est, 118, 3.
abbod-rīce, abbot-rīce, es; n. The rule of an abbot, an abbacy; abbatia :-- On his tīme wæx ðæt abbodrīce swīþe rīce in his time the abbacy waxed very rich, Chr. 656; Ing. 41, l.

expected_senses.gloss_en: The rule of an abbot, an abbacy

input_body: ā-beornan (-bi(e)rnan). Add: :-- Ābyrnð exardescit, Ps. L. 38, 4. Hē ābarn (exarsit) mid ðȳ bryne wælhreŎwnesse, Gr. D. 162, 22.

a-barian; . p. ede; pp. ed [a, barian to make bare; bær, se bara; adj. bare] To make bare, to manifest, discover, disclose; denudare, prodere, in medium proferre :-- Gif ðū abarast ūre sprǳce si sermonem nostrum profers in medium, Jos. 2, 20.

expected_senses.gloss_en: To make bare, to manifest, discover, disclose

input_body: ā-barian. Add: I. to make bare, strip :-- Stōwe rōde ābarude locum cruce denudatum, Angl. xiii. 427, 894. II. to lay bare, expose, disclose:-- Ælfremeda wunda nā ābarian (detegere) and geswutelian, R. Ben. I. 80, 12. Gylt ābarian delictum denudare, Scint. 195, 2.

ā-bǳdan. Substitute the following: I. to force, wring :-- Ele ābǳdan and āwringan of þām bergum ab olivis exigere oleum torquendo, Gr. D. 250, 22. II. to compel:-- Gif ðæt nȳd ābǳdeþcum exhiberi mysterium ipsa necessitas compellit, Bd. l, 27; S. 497, 1. III. to demand, require. (l) where the object is something needed :-- Nāniges fultumes ābǳdeþ siō lār nullum adjutorium expostulet ratio, Nar. 2, 2.

a-bannan; p. -beōnn, pl. -beōnnon ; pp. -bannen. I. to command, order, summon; mandare, jubere :-- Abannan to beadwe to summon to battle, Elen. Grm. 34. II. to publish, proclaim; with ūt to order out, call forth, call together, congregate, assemble; edicere, avocare, citare :-- Aban ðū ða beornas ūt of ofne command thou the men out of the oven, Cd. 193; Th. 242, 32; Dan. 428.

expected_senses.label: II
expected_senses.gloss_en: to publish, proclaim; with; to order out, call forth, call together, congregate, assemble

input_body: a-beran; p. -bær; pp. -boren. I. to bear, carry, suffer; portare, ferre :-- Ðe man aberan ne mæg which they are not able to bear, Mt. Bos. 23, 4. II. to take or carry away; tollere, auferre :-- Abær hine of eowdum sceāpa sustulit eam de gregibus ovium, Ps. Spl. 77, 76. v. beran.

ā-beran. Add: I. with sense of movement, (1) to bear off, bring, carry :-- Se hwæl hine ābær tō Ninuiēa birig, Ælfc. T. Grn. 10, 13. II. with sense of rest (metaph.). (1) to bear with, tolerate :-- Seō cyrice swā ābireþ.

abbadisse, abbodisse, abbatisse, abbudisse, abedisse, an; f. [abbad an abbot, isse a female termination, q. v.] An abbess; abbatissa :-- Riht is ðæt abbadissan fæste on mynstrum wunian it is right that abbesses dwell closely in their nunneries, L. I. P. 13; Th. ii. 320, 30.

abbad, abbod, abbud, abbot, es; m: abboda, an; m. I. an abbot; abbās, -- the title of the male superior of certain religious establishments. In point of dignity an abbot is generally next to a bishop :-- Se ārwurða abbad Albīnus the reverend abbot Albinus, Bd. pref. II. bishops were sometimes subject to an abbot, as they were to the abbots of Iona :-- Nū, sceal beōn ǳfre on Iī abbod, and nā biscop now, in Iī, there must ever be an abbot, not a bishop, Chr. 565.

expected_senses.label: II
expected_senses.gloss_en: bishops were sometimes subject to an abbot, as they were to the abbots of Iona

input_body: a-blīsian; p. ode; pp. od To blush; erubescere :-- ōþe eōwre lyþre mōd ablīsige donec erubescat incircumcisa mens eorum. Lev. 26,41.

a-belgan, ic -beige, ðū -bilgst, -bilhst, he -bylgþ, -bilhþ, pl. -belgaþ; p. -bealg, -bealh, pl. -bulgon; pp. -bolgen, v. trans. [a, belgan to irritate] To cause any one to swell with anger, to anger, irritate, vex, incense; ira aliquem tumefacere, irritare, exasperare, incendere :-- Ne sceal ic ðē abelgan I would not anger thee, Salm. Kmbl. 657; Sal. 328.

expected_senses.gloss_en: To cause any one to swell with anger, to anger, irritate, vex, incense

input_body: ā-beōdan. Add: (1) to announce, declare a message :-- Hē word ābeād he delivered the words of his message, B. 390. (2) to announce what is coming:-- Heāhengel hǳlo ābeād Marian. (3) to bid farewell:-- Hē hǳlo ābeād heorðgeneātum he bade farewell to his comrades, B. 2418.
ā-beatan. Add:-- Ic ðē ðīne tēþ of ābeāte, Lch. i. 326, 15.
ābēcēdē; f. An ABC, alphabet:-- Seō forme ābēcēdē on ðām gerīme ys būtan pricon.
abbod-leāst, e; f. Lack of an abbot:-- Ðæt mynstres þincȲ ne forwyrþан for abbudlēste ut non res monasterii abbatis privatione depereant, C. D. B. i. B. 155, 37.
abbud-dōm, es; m, [ = abbod-rīce, q. v.] An abbacy, the rule or authority of an abbot; abbātia, abbātis jus vel auctoritas :-- Abbuddōmes, gen. Bd. 5, 1; S. 613, 18.

expected_senses.gloss_en: An abbacy, the rule or authority of an abbot

input_body: abbud-hād, es; m. The state or dignity of an abbot; abbatis dignitas :-- Munuchād and abbudhād ne syndon getealde to ðysum getele monkhood and abbothood are not reckoned in this number, L. Ælf. C. 18; Th. ii. 348, 31.

expected_senses.gloss_en: The state or dignity of an abbot

input_body: a-beoflan To be moved or shaken, to tremble; moveri, contremere :-- Ealle abeofedan eorþian staðalas movebuntur omnia fundamenta terrae, Ps. Th. 81, 5. v. beofian.

expected_senses.gloss_en: To be moved or shaken, to tremble

input_body: a-beden asked, Nicod. 12; Thw. 6, 15: Bd. 4, 10; S. 578, 31; pp. of a-biddan.
a-bēgendlīc; adj. Bending; flexibilis, Som. v. a-bēgan.
a-behōfian; p. ode To behove, concern; decere :-- Mid māran unrǳde ðone him abehōfode with more animosity than it behoved him, Chr. 1093; Th. 360, 4. v. be-hōfian.
a-beāg bowed down, Beo. Th. 1555; B. 775; p. of a-būgan.

ā-barian. Add: I. to make bare, strip :-- Stōwe rōde ābarude locum cruce denudatum, Angl. xiii. 427, 894. II. to lay bare, expose, disclose:-- Ælfremeda wunda nā ābarian (detegere) and geswutelian, R. Ben. I. 80, 12. For ābaredum ob detectum, Hpt. Gl. 474, 78.
ā-belgan.. Add:-- Ābealg exacerbavit, provocavit, adflixit, Wrt. Voc. ii. 144, 56. Ābulge offenderet, 63, 4.

ā-beran. Add: I. with sense of movement, (1) to bear off, bring, carry :-- Se hwæl hine ābær tō Ninuiēa birig. (2) to bring forth, (a) to bear a child :-- Ðæt bearn ðe ābær ūrne Hǳlend, Hml. A. 25, 16. II. with sense of rest (metaph.). (1) to bear with, tolerate :-- Seō cyrice swā ābireþ. (2) to bear, endure :-- Hē ðā wītu ābær.
abbad-dōm an abbacy, v. abbud-dōm.
abbad-hād the state or dignity of an abbot, v. abbud-hād.

expected_senses.gloss_en: the state or dignity of an abbot

input_body: abbod an abbot, L. I. P. 13; Th. ii. 320, 30. v. abbad.
abboda, an; m. An abbot; abbās :-- Swā gebireþ abbodan as becometh abbots, L. I. P. 13; Th. ii. 320, 35. v. abbad.
abbud an abbot. Chr. 803; Erl. 60, 13: Bd. 5, 23; S. 645, 14. v. abbad.
abbudisse, an; m. An abbess :-- Ðā sealde seō abbudisse him sumne dǳl ðǳre moldan tunc dedit ei abbatissa portiunculam de pulvere illo, Bd. 3, 11; S. 536, 38. v. abbadisse.
agenness. Substitute: A property :-- Seō sunne hæfd dreō āgen-nyssa on hire. Hml. Th. i. 282, 8.
ā-beatan. Add:-- Ic ðē ðīne tēþ of ābeāte, Lch. i. 326, 15.
ā-barian. Add: I. to strip bare :-- Stōwe rōde ābarude locum cruce denudatum, Angl. 427. II. to expose, disclose :-- Gylt ābarian delictum denudare, Scint. 195, 2.
a-bacan to bake:-- Nim ǳlces cynnes melo and ābacæ man hlāf, Lch. i. 404, 5. Ðost tō cicle ābacen, 364, 15.
a-bād expected, waited :-- And abād swā ðeāh seofon dagas expectavitque nihilominus septem alios dies, Gen. 8, 12. v. abīdan.
a-bǳdan; p. -bǳdde; pp. -bǳded To restrain, repel, compel; avertere, repellere, cogere, exigere :-- Is fira ǳnig, ðe deāþ abǳde is there any man, who can restrain death ? Salm. Kmbl. 957; Sal. 478.
a-bær bore or took away; sustulit, Ps. Spl. 77, 76; p. of a-beran.
abbodisse. Add:-- Seō abbodyssa, Lch. iii. 428, 16. Abbodesse, L. In. 23 ; Th. i. 118, 1. Abbudesse, Chr. 805; Erl. 60, 17.
ā-lūcan. Add: :-- Up ālūcþ eradicat, extirpat, Wrt. Voc. ii. 144, 19. Ūt ālūcþ evellit, i. eradicat, 32.
ā-beligan. v. ā-bilgan.
ā-beōwed. v. ā-bīwan.
ā-beofian. v. ā-bifian.
ā-lūcan. Add: :-- Up ālūcþ eradicat, extirpat, Wrt. Voc. ii. 144, 19.
aam, es; m. A reed of a weaver's loom. Exon. 109 a; Th. 417, 22 ; Rä. 36, 8; Cod. Lugd. Grn. v. ām.

expected_senses.gloss_en: A reed of a weaver's loom

input_body: blinnan; part. blinnende; ic blinne, ðū blinnest, blinst, he blinneþ, blinniþ, blinþ, pl. blinnaþ; p. ic, he blan, blon, blann, blonn, ðū blunne, pl. blunnon; pp. blunnen; v. intrans. [be, linnan to cease] To cease, rest, leave off; cessare, desinere :-- Seō rēþnes ðæs stormes wæs blinnende the fierceness of the storm ceased [lit. was ceasing], Bd. 5, 1; S. 614, 9.
ād-loma, -lama? an; m. One crippled by the flame? cui flamma claudicationem attulit? -- Earme ādloman poor wretches, i.e. diaboli, Exon. 46a; Th. 156, 33; Gū. 884.
